items.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Jimmy Vass was also another one. Him and Archie were close.

ctx.x: Yeah, you had to because blues singers had a lot of the gigs. If you wanted to get the jobs . . . If people wanted to throw a party, they may use a local club to do that because there were drinks there and they may even get a caterer to cater to it. So all of that was a part of it and I enjoyed participating in that. People would come and have a good time, you know? And then I would do some gigs with Lee and Archie every now and then.
Jimmy Vass was also another one. Him and Archie were close.

Yeah, Sure were. There were a lot of young people . . . There were so many guys around, it’s hard to name them all. In my mind, I have to leave some room for music, I think that’s important! [laughs] All these dates, I mean they’re fine but-
